column11: No sensor is read. The function has two parts. (1) It clears parameter_block_uploaded and loads a flash parameter block. When both marker words 0x55B2 and 0x75B2 hold 0xA1A1, it loads block 1 and clears the RAM copy of the marker at 0x806548. Otherwise it picks the newest complete block from the save start / complete counts and the odd / even sum of the two start counts (cm550_loadParameterBlock1FromFlash / cm550_loadParameterBlock2FromFlash), with the other block as fallback. When no block loaded, it sets status word 0 bit 0x1000 (all power-down data lost) and its first-occurrence bit. engine_startup_inhibit_true_false = 1 while that bit is set, confirmed (0x806abc bit 0x1000) and 0x808484 = 0. (2) It does the start-up power-down bookkeeping that CM848 does inline in cm848_applicationMain, in the same order. If power_cycle_sequence_number_cal = completed_power_down_sequence_number_cal: consecutive count <- 0, completed count +1, clear bit 0x800. Otherwise: consecutive count +1, incomplete count +1, and bit 0x800 is set when the consecutive count is above 0x808480. Last: sequence number <- completed + incomplete. Each write goes through cm550_parameterCircularBufferWrite and waits up to 5000 passes of 500 timebase ticks (CM848: 5000 passes), with interrupts enabled (andi #0xf1ff,sr) around the wait. mc68k_applicationMain calls it once, right before its inline flash_write_failure_flag_cal and 0x803fda checks; that is CM848's order. Prefix cm550_: no CM848 function does this, because the CM848 bookkeeping is inline code. The CM848 inline code also sets fault_detected_cal.power_off_without_ignition_off_error and high_idle_override_flag, which this function does not, so it is a counterpart, not a twin. It accesses no MC68336 module register (only SR for the interrupt mask, as cm550_savePowerDownDataToFlashBank does) and nothing VP44-related.

This is the boot ROM's software-restart entry: a point inside the body of mc68k_hardwareInitAndStartup that has its own function row, like cm550_restartApplicationWithoutReset (0x28978) inside mc68k_applicationMain. How it is reached: (a) restartThroughBootRom (0x1192a, twin of CM848 0x216fc) masks interrupts, sets SP to 0x811000, loads the long at ROM 0x8 and jumps to it. (b) The cold path falls into it: reset PC 0x1e (SIM / clock / chip selects) -> jsr 0x3a94, which writes the chip select 2 device (0xffd008 = 0x40, 0xffd00e = 0x80), waits for the chip select 2 input bit 0 (mc68k_waitForChipSelect2InputBit0High), sets port E bit 3, and then runs on into 0x3abe. So the warm entry skips exactly those steps. What it does from 0x3abe: stops the QSPI (SPSR &0x7f, SPCR1 &0x7fff, SPCR2 &0x7fff / &0xfff0); clears QILR / SCCR1, PICR / PITR, TPU_CIER and the QADC registers; resets and configures CTM4 (BIUMCR 0x1601, CPCR 8, MCSM11SIC 4, FCSM12SIC 0x104); sets QSMCR 5 / QILR 0x13 / QIVR 0x50; clears RAM (cm550_ramClearWithWatchdog). Then it starts the Huffman-decompressed RAM kernel at 0x80339e when mc68k_portPinTestSequence2 returns 1 or the serial EEPROM signature is not 0x600d. Otherwise it starts the application through the long at 0x8062 when the 0x8000 header is 0x98765432 / 0x98765433 (dump: 0x98765432 -> 0x1dbee), or else through the long at 0x20000. mc68k_ because it writes MC68336 module registers. Counterpart, not a twin, of CM848 mpc555_hardwareInitialization (0x2694). Matches: the QSPI stop constants, the 0x600d EEPROM check, a four-pin QADC strap test, the kernel-or-application ending, and a pointer word right after the reset vector (CM550 0x8 / CM848 0x104) that the twin restartThroughBootRom jumps through. Differences: CM848 adds BR0-3 / OR0-3 / SIUMCR, the MIOS counter set-up, the TPU module stop and the flash2 identification. CM550 adds PICR / PITR, the CTM4 block and QSMCR / QILR / QIVR. CM550 tests the pins before it reads the EEPROM; CM848 reads the EEPROM first. CM550 selects the program by the 0x8000 signature and 0x8062; CM848 jumps through flash_operational_code_entry_pointer. CM848's is a whole function with three call sites; CM550's is a mid-body entry. This follows the precedent of mc68k_waitForChipSelect2InputBit0High / mc68k_checkSerialEepromSignature, which have 'same pattern as CM848' notes and kept mc68k_.

This is the same record as CM848's power_down_left_ecm_powered_flag_cal: e2m 1069 SDENER 'a status indicator saved to EEPROM indicating power was commanded off and is still on' (CM848 Poweroff_Command_Ignored). It sits at CM550 1069 +6 (CM848 +4): CM550's own table puts 1069 at EEPROM 0x4CA = mirror 0x803fd4, and 64t6.e2m has PDBLKSPT at +0, which shifts every CM848 1069 offset by 2. It has the same writers and reader as in CM848. mc68k_runPowerDownSequence writes 0 after it saves the hour meters and before it clears output request bit 3 of 0x80bcf8 and strobes the outputs. It writes 1 when the ECM is still running after the 40 x 500-tick window, the re-set of bit 3 and the 4 x 10000-tick delays with the key still off. Each write waits up to 1000 passes. At the next start mc68k_applicationMain sets status word 0 bit 0x400 and its first-occurrence bit while the flag is non-zero, and clears bit 0x400 otherwise. CM848: cm848_runPowerDownSequence writes 0 / 1 around logical output 27, and cm848_applicationMain sets fault bit 0x800. Every access is a word (.w, 2-byte writes). It is in the EEPROM mirror, so _cal. 0 in the RAM and EEPROM dumps.

Same record as CM848's power_cycle_sequence_number_cal (0x3fdc88): e2m 1069 SDRMIMSR (Parameter_Block_Image_Start), at CM550 1069 +E (CM848 +C). It has the three uses CM848 has. At every start 0x114d4 writes it as incomplete + completed count and compares it with 0x803fe4 to see whether the previous power-down completed. restartOnKeyOnDuringPowerDown rewrites it as completed + incomplete after it adds 1 to the completed count. cm550_savePowerDownDataToFlashBank copies it into 0x803fe4 after the flash save (CM848: cm848_saveEepromForPowerDown). Every access is a word. In the EEPROM mirror, so _cal. The dump identity holds: 10193 = 0x803fea 89 + 0x803fec 10104.

Same record as CM848's completed_power_down_sequence_number_cal (0x3fdc8a): e2m 1069 SDRMIMCP (Parameter_Block_Image_Complete), at CM550 1069 +10 (CM848 +E). cm550_savePowerDownDataToFlashBank writes power_cycle_sequence_number_cal into it once the parameter block save is done, as cm848_saveEepromForPowerDown does. At start, 0x114d4 counts the previous power-down as completed when the two are equal. Every access is a word. In the EEPROM mirror, so _cal. The dump holds 10168 while the running cycle is 10193.

Same record as CM848's consecutive_incomplete_power_down_count_cal (0x3fdc8c): e2m 1069 SDDLCU 'number of consecutive occurances of powerdown data lost, updated each powerup', at CM550 1069 +12 (CM848 +10). Only 0x114d4 uses it. It is set to 0 after a completed power-down and +1 after an incomplete one. When it is above consecutive_incomplete_power_down_limit (0x808480), status word 0 bit 0x800 is set; otherwise the bit is cleared. This is CM848's branch structure and test. Every access is a word. In the EEPROM mirror, so _cal. Observed in the dump: 23, with limit 0 and bit 0x800 set in 0x806000 (0x2800).

Same record as CM848's incomplete_power_down_count_cal (0x3fdc90 = 106A +0 Reset_Count): e2m 106A +0 NRESETSE 'cumulative count of non-power up resets'. CM550's table puts 106A at EEPROM 0x4E0 = 0x803fea. 0x114d4 adds 1 to it when the previous power-down did not complete. 0x114d4 and restartOnKeyOnDuringPowerDown add it to the completed count to form the sequence number, as in CM848. Every access is a word. In the EEPROM mirror, so _cal. Dump 89.

Same record as CM848's completed_power_down_count_cal (0x3fdc92): e2m 106A +2 SSPURSCU 'cumulative count of power cycles' (CM848 Powerup_Count). It has the same two writers as in CM848. 0x114d4 adds 1 at a start after a completed power-down. restartOnKeyOnDuringPowerDown (twin of CM848 0x539938) adds 1 before the restart. Nothing VP44- or reset-related touches it. Every access is a word. In the EEPROM mirror, so _cal. Dump 10104.

e2m 1069 +8 SDEEWRFU 'a status indicator saved to EEPROM indicating a failure of one or more EEPROM cells to program' (CM848 1069 +6 EEPROM_Failed_To_Program, 0x3fdc82; no CM848 row and no reference in the frozen CM848 .cpp). The name parallels its neighbour flash_write_failure_flag_cal (1069 +14). It has one reader: the power-down step at 0x30a5e. That step runs first in mc68k_runPowerDownSequence and sets bits 0x2 and 0x80 of the dword 0x80614e when calibration_feature_enable_flags_word_3 bit 0x200 is set and this word is non-zero. The dumped 256 KB has no absolute-long reference that writes it. Word (tst.w). In the EEPROM mirror, so _cal. 0 in the RAM and EEPROM dumps.

Same record as CM848's consecutive_incomplete_power_down_limit (0x645ba): e2m 122A +0 SDDLERLM 'number of consecutive occurances of powerdown data lost to set (system error)'. CM550's table maps 122A -> 0x808480. 0x114d4 compares it with consecutive_incomplete_power_down_count_cal and sets status word 0 bit 0x800 when the count is above it; this is CM848's 'limit < count' test. It is a RAM copy of the ROM calibration (copyCalibrationFromRomToRam fills 0x80654a-0x808acd), not EEPROM, so no _cal. Word (cmp.w). Observed RAM dump value 0, which is outside the e2m range of 1-255.

e2m 122A +2 SDFHPNEA 'enable to protects parameter block data at powerdown' (CM848 e2m Parameter_Block_Protection_Enable, 'ENABLE=preserve 1 block'; no CM848 row). Its only reader is cm550_savePowerDownDataToFlashBank. When all 3 attempts on the first block fail, that function sets flash_write_failure_flag_cal = 1, and it writes the other block too only while this word is 0. A non-zero value therefore keeps the other block intact, which matches the e2m text. Word (tst.w). RAM calibration copy, so no _cal. RAM dump 1.

e2m 122A +4 SSDXLTRN 'flag indicating if engine should be ran if All_Powerdown_Data_Lost_Error is true' (CM848 e2m All_Powerdown_Data_Lost_Run; no CM848 row). 0x114d4 reads it twice. While it is 0, a confirmed all-power-down-data-lost error (status word 0 bit 0x1000) stays set even after a block loads, and engine_startup_inhibit_true_false = 1. While it is non-zero, the engine is allowed to start and the bit clears once a block loads. Word (tst.w). RAM calibration copy, so no _cal. RAM dump 1.

It holds the value that 0x114d4 queues for each EEPROM write of the bookkeeping words; CM848 uses a stack local (local_20) for the same purpose. Its only references are 0x114d4's two movea.l #0x8001d2 into a2 and a5. The function writes the new value through a2 (move.w d0,(a2) / clr.w (a2)), passes a5 as the source pointer of each 2-byte cm550_parameterCircularBufferWrite, and compares the mirror word with (a2) while it waits. No hour meter code touches it. The RAM dump holds 0x27d1 = 10193, the sequence number that is the last value written. Word; working RAM, so no _cal.

TWIN of CM848 0x21a24 cm848_registerJ1939DiagnosticHandlers (one shared name; the CM848 row follows). Same steps in the same order: 8 calls of the same registration helper (0x2ee62, the twin of CM848 0x220e4) with the same service constants 1, 7, 10, 22, 6, 11, 24, 21 and the corresponding handlers (services 7/10/22/11 are already shared twins). Same role in the start-up graph: called from the J1939 datalink init right before the registrar of services 15/16/4/5 in both firmwares. The live CM550 table holds the same 8 pairs as entries 12-19, after the memory read (0-4), get-address (5) and memory write (6-11) services, which is CM848's registrar call order too. Two of the eight handlers it registers (services 1 and 21) are counterparts, not twins (see their rows). The twin claim rests on the registrar's own code: the same helper, constants, order and call site.

TWIN of CM550 0x11b36 (see the CM550 row): the same 8 registrations (services 1, 7, 10, 22, 6, 11, 24, 21) through the twin helper, in the same order and at the same place in the J1939 start-up. Two of the registered handlers (services 1 and 21) are counterparts; the twin claim rests on the registrar's own code. One shared unprefixed name.

TWIN of CM848 0x220e4 cm848_j1939RegisterDiagnosticService (one shared name; the CM848 row follows). The same steps: it returns 1 when the count byte is 32; otherwise entry = table + count * 6, count + 1, entry byte 0 = the service, entry + 2 = the handler (long), and it returns 0. The table layout is the same: 32 x 6-byte entries directly followed by the count byte (CM550 0x801c7a + 0xc0 = 0x801d3a; CM848 0x3fa8b2 + 0xc0 = 0x3fa972). The name is verb-first like the registrars that call it and like CM848's receive-side twin cm848_registerJ1939ReceiveHandler. The frozen .cpp has no block for this function. The exporter skips functions that fail to decompile, but the cause is not established here (no deleted_functions.csv or function_definitions.csv row for 0x2ee62). A suggestion: add a function_definitions prototype (byte return; word service_id, 2-byte slot with its low byte stored; pointer handler) so that the registrars' calls show their arguments.

TWIN of CM550 0x2ee62 (see the CM550 row): the same full check at 32, 6-byte entry, count increment, service byte at +0, handler long at +2, return 1 / 0, and the same table + count layout. One shared name, verb-first like registerJ1939DiagnosticHandlers and cm848_registerJ1939ReceiveHandler. Other CM848 comments that cite cm848_j1939RegisterDiagnosticService (for example cm848_registerJ1939ReceiveHandler's 'receive side twin of ...') need the new name.

TWIN of CM848 0x216e8 cm848_commandEngineShutdown (one shared name; the CM848 row follows). Both store word 1 in the e2m 10B1 +12 SHSS record ('TURN OFF ALL SOLENOIDS': engine_shutdown_command_flag) and return 0, as service 6, fifth in the same registrar. Nothing in it tests rpm, so the old high-rpm name is wrong. CM550 also reaches it as J1708 command 66.

TWIN of CM550 0x118fc (see the CM550 row): the same single word store of 1 into the e2m 10B1 +12 SHSS record and the same return 0, registered as service 6 in the twin registrar. One shared unprefixed name.

TWIN of CM848 0x21904 cm848_inhibitKeyOffShutdown (one shared name; the CM848 row follows). Both store word 1 in key_off_shutdown_inhibit_flag (CM550 0x80de2e, the same record; see its global row) and return 0, as service 24, seventh in the same registrar. CM550 also reaches it as J1708 command 82.

TWIN of CM550 0x11a68 (see the CM550 row): the same single word store of 1 into the key-off shutdown inhibit record and the same return 0, registered as service 24 in the twin registrar. One shared unprefixed name.

COUNTERPART, NOT A TWIN, of CM848 0x21584 cm848_requestClearInactiveFaults. The step is the same: the CLEAR_INACTIVE bit of e2m 1080 +2 DGJCFUCC (diagnostic_clear_request_state) goes 0 -> 1, 1 -> 1, 2 -> 3, 3 -> 3. The results are the same: 0 accepted, 7 not safe. The acceptance gate differs. CM550 accepts only not_safe_to_program_flag == 2, which CM550 writes for engine_state 1 with key switch bit 0 on (J90350.00.ghidra.cpp:11674-11685). CM848 accepts (flag 0 and the key switch on) or (flag 1 and algorithm_enable_flags_12_cal.obd_fault_handler_enable 0), and CM848's periodic writer cm848_updateNotSafeToProgramFlag stores 0 / 1. The verdict does not depend on that writer: the extra OBD branch alone makes the code differ. The function touches no MC68336 register and is not VP44 code, so it takes the cm550_ prefix.

COUNTERPART, NOT A TWIN, of CM848 0x21918; this reverses round 73's shared name. The mirror loop is the same: 7 while not_safe_to_program_flag is 1; 16-byte chunks to the EEPROM write queue; two failed queue writes end it; up to 16000 waits per chunk; power_down_refresh_enable = 0 on success. The answer to the requester differs, which is more than a different address. On success CM550 arms a deferred J1708 reply (0x80dde4 = 1, which mc68k_dispatchJ1708ReceivedMessages sends once the EEPROM queue is empty) and returns 0xff, so its J1939 dispatcher sends no response frame. CM848 returns 0 (J1939_DIAGNOSTIC_RESULT_ACCEPTED, a positive response). On failure CM550 also clears byte 0x80ddd3 before it returns 11. CM550 also reaches it as J1708 command 84. Its current comment ends in '; 0.', which is wrong: success returns 0xff and failure returns 11. No MC68336 register access, so the prefix is cm550_. Comments that cite the shared name need the new names in both firmwares: CM550 mc68k_dispatchJ1708ReceivedMessages (function_renames.csv:174), CM848 cm848_updateNotSafeToProgramFlag (function_renames.csv:1024) and the CM848 enums.csv:510 member comment.

COUNTERPART, NOT A TWIN, of CM550 0x11a74 (see the CM550 row). CM848's version answers the J1939 request on success (result 0) and has no deferred reply flag. CM550's version arms a J1708 reply and returns 0xff (no J1939 answer), and it also clears 0x80ddd3 on failure. This restores the pre-round-73 name. The comments that cite the shared name (CM848 cm848_updateNotSafeToProgramFlag, function_renames.csv:1024, and the enums.csv:510 member comment) need the new name.

The same record as CM848's key_off_shutdown_inhibit_flag (0x40aa98). It is set to 1 only by service 24 (inhibitKeyOffShutdown). The engine_state machine moves to state 8 (shutdown) on a key-off only while it is 0, and the power-down start in state 8 also waits for it. It is cleared on the key-on rising edge. Those are the same three uses as in cm848_updateEngineState. It sits 2 bytes below development_mode (e2m 1328 +0) in both firmwares: CM550 0x80de30 (parameter ID table entry at ROM 0x36cdc = 00 80 de 30), CM848 0x40aa9a. It is working RAM outside the EEPROM mirror 0x803b0a-0x804155, so it takes no _cal. The global_variables.csv row 5739 has an empty name.

e2m 10B1 +12 SHSS ('TURN OFF ALL SOLENOIDS. 1=TRUE ; 0=FALSE'), the record CM848 names engine_shutdown_command_flag (0x40a784 = 0x40a772 + 0x12). It is set by service 6 (commandEngineShutdown) and by the engine protection code. At 1 it moves engine_state to 8 (shutdown), and it is cleared at engine speed 0 in state 8, as in CM848. Every access is a word. Its type is undefined now, which is why it renders as _engine_protection_shutdown_command.

e2m 1080 +2 DGJCFUCC ('00=NO_CLEAR_ACTION 01=CLEAR_INACTIVE 02=CLEAR_ACTIVE 03=CLEAR_ALL'), the record CM848 names diagnostic_clear_request_state (e2m 1080 +2 DL_to_Fault_Handler_Command). Service 1 (cm550_requestClearInactiveFaults) sets its CLEAR_INACTIVE bit, and cm550_FUN_00014812 acts on it and clears it, as CM848's clear processing does. Every access is a word.

A new CM550 type with CM848's layout and field names (CM848 structure_definitions.csv rows 1160-1162). The registration helper stores the service byte at +0 and the handler long at +2 and never writes +1. The dispatcher compares +0 with the request's first data byte and calls through +2. CM550's J1939_DIAGNOSTIC_SERVICE enum is 1 byte. It is needed for the table global row.

CM848's j1939_diagnostic_service_table (0x3fa8b2, j1939_diagnostic_service_entry_t[32]): the PGN 61184 service table that registerJ1939DiagnosticService appends to (at most 32) and cm550_diagnosticServiceDispatcher scans. 0x801c7a + 32 * 6 = 0x801d3a, the count byte, which is CM848's layout too. It has no global_variables.csv row now. The neighbours do not overlap: 0x801c78 remote_throttle_active_flag (1 byte) and 0x801d44.

CM848's j1939_diagnostic_handler_count (0x3fa972, byte): the entry count of j1939_diagnostic_service_table, compared with 32 and incremented by the registration helper and used as the scan bound by the dispatcher. It sits directly after the 32-entry table in both firmwares. The CM550 dump holds 24, and CM848's row comment says its live value is 24. It has no global_variables.csv row now.

A CM550-only flag (CM848's commit has none). cm550_commitEepromMirrorToEeprom sets it to 1 after the whole mirror is queued. mc68k_dispatchJ1708ReceivedMessages tests it first on each pass and, once the EEPROM write queue is empty, clears it and writes the reply (cm550_diagnosticMessageQueueWrite(0), the J1708 transmit ring per round 87's restartThroughBootRom note). It is working RAM outside the EEPROM mirror, so it takes no _cal. The global_variables.csv row 5719 has an empty name.

CM848's member name for service 1. The service does the same job in both firmwares: it sets the CLEAR_INACTIVE bit of e2m 1080 +2. Only the acceptance gate of the handler differs, so the handler is a counterpart (cm550_requestClearInactiveFaults), but the member names the service. No query or terminate happens. The row's comment should name 0x1183e cm550_requestClearInactiveFaults.

CM848's member name for service 4. CM550's handler 0x200a4 calls 0x1ffd6(request, 0), which clears the request's item bits in the J1939 broadcast enable word (_bit_2_0_15_enables_j1939_71_engine_broadcast_1_on_0_off). The item / target constants match CM848's cm848_updateJ1939BroadcastEnableMask, and CM848's 0x509ce4 passes 0 the same way. The row's comment 'NOT in dispatch table' is wrong: the live table holds it as entry 22.

CM848's member name for service 5. CM550's handler 0x200b4 calls 0x1ffd6(request, 1), which sets the request's item bits in the J1939 broadcast enable word, as CM848's 0x509d0c does through cm848_updateJ1939BroadcastEnableMask(request, 1). The row's comment 'NOT in dispatch table' is wrong: the live table holds it as entry 23.

CM848's member name for service 6. The handler is the twin commandEngineShutdown (0x118fc), which sets the e2m 10B1 +12 SHSS shutdown command. There is no rpm test. The row's comment should name commandEngineShutdown.

CM848's member name for service 7. The handler is the twin exitDevelopmentMode (0x1188c, shared since round 73), re-checked. Only while development_mode is 1 does it clear development_mode, set ram_refresh_enable 1 and set run_location 0xeeee, and return 0; otherwise it returns 4.

CM848's member name for service 10. The handler is the twin enterDevelopmentMode (0x118b2), re-checked. It sets ram_refresh_enable 0, development_mode 1 and run_location 0xeaea, and returns 0. CM550 also reaches it as J1708 command 64.

CM848's member name for service 15. CM550's handler 0x1ffd2 is clr.b d0; rts: it is accepted and does nothing, like CM848's cm848_j1939DiagnosticServiceAcknowledgeNoOperation (li r3,0; blr). That explains the bench note 'RESPONDS!'. It reads no parameters, and the live table holds it (entry 20).

CM848's member name for service 16. It uses the same no-operation handler 0x1ffd2 as service 15 (accepted, does nothing), as CM848 registers 16 to the same no-operation handler. The live table holds it (entry 21).

CM848's member name for service 21. Its handler commits the EEPROM mirror in both firmwares. The handler is a counterpart because of the reply path (cm550_commitEepromMirrorToEeprom), but the service's job is the same. GET_ADDRESS_BY_PARAM_ID is service 0x41 (live entry 5, handler 0x222b4), not 0x15.

CM848's member name for service 22. The handler is the twin forceExitDevelopmentMode (0x118cc), re-checked. It returns 7 while not_safe_to_program_flag is 1. Otherwise it sets ram_refresh_enable 1 and, if run_location is 0xeaea, sets 0xeeee and clears development_mode, and returns 0. CM550 also reaches it as J1708 command 65.

CM848's member name for service 24. The handler is the twin inhibitKeyOffShutdown (0x11a68), which sets key_off_shutdown_inhibit_flag. The enum header's '# Dispatch table: 20 entries' comment should say 24: the dump's count byte is 0x18.

This is the engine state update, not a VP44 timing fault monitor. (1) The engine overspeed latch: while engine_rpm_primary is at or above engine_overspeed_set_rpm_threshold for more than engine_overspeed_debounce_limit passes, it sets engine_overspeed_active_flag, fault word 2 bit 15 and opens an engine_overspeed_log record; below engine_overspeed_clear_rpm_threshold it clears the flag, writes the duration and moves engine_overspeed_log_index on (modulo 5). (2) The FSEGST state machine on engine_state (1 STOP ... 8 SHUTDOWN, default -> 1). (3) It clears key_off_shutdown_inhibit_flag on a key-on edge and saves the key state. COUNTERPART, NOT A TWIN of CM848 cm848_updateEngineState: the overspeed block, the 8 states, the transition order and the static layout (word / byte / byte) are the same. CM848 adds steps CM550 does not have: the engine_state_crank_time / engine_state_run_time captures, engine_is_active_flag / engine_is_starting_flag, and the ecm_power_down_timer / delay / delay-request logic (CM550 sets power_down_start_flag directly). CM550 leaves ENGINE_BRAKE only when engine_retarder_active_flag AND engine_brake_driveline_brake_type_cal are both 0. The fault bookkeeping differs too: CM550 sets two words and clears one, CM848 sets one and clears two. It has no MC68336 peripheral access (only the CPU status-register interrupt mask) and nothing VP44-specific, so the prefix is cm550_.

TWIN of CM848 0x1c978 (cm848_initCrankingLimits). Both do the same 3 stores in the same order with the same widths and constants: key_off_shutdown_mode (e2m 120C +4) = 0, engine_state = 1 (STOPPED), engine_state_key_on_previous_flag = 0. Both are called once from the application main's start-up init list. One shared unprefixed name.

The twin rename of CM550 0x18384. It sets no cranking limits: it stores key_off_shutdown_mode = 0, engine_state = ENGINE_STATE_STOPPED and mios_timer_active_flag (engine_state_key_on_previous_flag) = 0. Comments that cite the old name: key_off_shutdown_mode (global_variables.csv 0x40a334, 'written only by cm848_initCrankingLimits').

This is the RAM refresh initializer, and it does nothing with CAN. It fills two 12-byte (RAM start, RAM end, source) refresh blocks at 0x801c4e. Block 1 is RAM 0x80654a-0x808acc from ROM 0x61376 (the copyCalibrationFromRomToRam ranges). Block 2 is RAM 0x806544-0x806546 from 0x55ae (block 1) or 0x75ae (block 2, when parameter_block_uploaded = 2); that is the tail word of the flash parameter block (flash 0x4004 / 0x6004 + 0x15aa). It sums the words, sets the per-pass chunk to total / 20 + 1, points the cursors at block 1, clears the rewrite flag, and sets ram_refresh_enable = RAM_REFRESH_ENABLED, power_down_refresh_enable = 1 and the previous-enable word = 1. COUNTERPART, NOT A TWIN of CM848 cm848_initializeRamRefresh: CM848 fills one block (0x3feed0-0x40a046 from ROM 0x64aea) and uses a fixed 100-byte chunk. CM550 also calls it after each flash parameter block save. No hardware access, so cm550_.

This is the RAM refresh pass. It re-initializes on an enable edge and turns the refresh off while parameter_block_uploaded is 0. While the refresh is on, it walks the refresh blocks (it skips block 2 while power_down_refresh_enable is 0, which matches the RRPWEA text) and compares up to words-per-pass words with their source, rewriting each RAM word that differs. At the end of each cycle it sets fault word 0 bit 1 (status and first-occurrence words) if any word was rewritten, or clears it when it is set and not yet first-occurrence. COUNTERPART, NOT A TWIN of CM848 cm848_refreshRamCalibration: CM848 has one block and fixed 100-byte steps, never reads power_down_refresh_enable, counts sensor_cal_ring_cycle_count, clears fault bit 0 on the enable edge and uses fault bit 0 (P0606), not bit 1. The call graph differs as well: CM550 runs it in executive interrupt phase 31, CM848 in the application main's background loop.

The engine overspeed latch, the same role and static slot as CM848 engine_overspeed_active_flag (0x3fa863, byte). It is set when the debounce passes engine_overspeed_debounce_limit and cleared below engine_overspeed_clear_rpm_threshold. While it is 1, RUNNING moves to OVERSPEED, and OVERSPEED returns to RUNNING when it is 0. Nothing in it is VP44-specific.

The count of passes in a row with engine_rpm_primary at or above engine_overspeed_set_rpm_threshold. It is zeroed below the threshold and when the latch sets. Same role and static slot as CM848 engine_overspeed_debounce_count (0x3fa860, word). Only this function touches it.

The key switch state (SWITCHES bit 0, e2m 000E DSKYSWSS 'status of the vehicle key switch - debounced') saved at the end of each engine state pass. A 0 -> 1 change (a key-on edge) clears key_off_shutdown_inhibit_flag. initializeEngineState zeroes it. CM848 holds the same thing at 0x3fa862 (renamed in the CM848 row). The name follows the existing <owner>_key_on_previous_flag pattern (fuel_level_low_distance_check_key_on_previous_flag).

This is not a MIOS timer flag. It holds the ignition key line (mios_mdasm30.SCRD bit 15) at the end of the last cm848_updateEngineState pass, and a 0 -> 1 change clears key_off_shutdown_inhibit_flag. initializeEngineState (was cm848_initCrankingLimits) zeroes it. The CM550 twin slot 0x8005fc has the same role. A whole-binary sweep finds only these two users.

e2m 1032 +0 FSOSLMES 'engine speed max. used by software to lock fuel to overspeed' (RPM, 0.125), the same record as CM848 engine_overspeed_set_rpm_threshold. It has nothing to do with intake manifold temperature. CM550's table maps 1032 to 0x807f1c. The dump value is 28000 = 3500 rpm.

e2m 1032 +2 FSOSHYES 'engine overspeed limit hysteresis', the same record as CM848 engine_overspeed_clear_rpm_threshold. The code compares the speed with it directly (an absolute clear speed): below it, the overspeed latch clears. The dump value is 24000 = 3000 rpm. It has nothing to do with throttle position.

e2m 1032 +4 FSOSEN 'time before triggering engine overspeed' (MSEC, 20 per count), the same record as CM848 engine_overspeed_debounce_limit. The latch needs the debounce count to exceed it. The dump value is 3, the same as CM848's.

e2m 1032 +6 CKSPRP 'engine speed for transition into/out of crank (reentry) state', the same record as CM848 engine_stopped_speed (Engine_Stopped_Speed [CKSPRP]). STOPPED -> CRANKING happens above it, and CRANKING / JUMP_START / REENTRY -> STOPPED happens at or below it. The dump value is 80 = 10 rpm.

New CM550 type with the same layout and field names as CM848's engine_overspeed_event_t, for the 8-byte records of the engine overspeed log (DGRPOSLF). +0 is the key_on_hour_meter value when the record opens. +4 is the highest engine_rpm_primary seen while it is open. +6 is the duration: the low word of key_on_hour_meter minus the low word of +0, written when the overspeed clears. The engine_overspeed_log struct_instance row depends on this row.

e2m 10DA +0 DGRPOSLF 'fault log for engine speed overspeed conditions' (40 bytes), the same record as CM848 engine_overspeed_log_cal. CM550's table maps 10DA to 0x80553a. No _cal: it is in the flash parameter block (RAM 0x804f9a-0x806547, saved to flash 0x4004 / 0x6004 at power-down), not the EEPROM mirror 0x803b0a-0x804155. Flag this for the orchestrator. Only this function touches 0x80553a-0x805561. Depends on the engine_overspeed_event_t struct_type row. Delete the 18 interior rows: 0x0080553b diagnostic_snapshot_limited_byte, 0x0080553c diagnostic_snapshot_fuel_mode_0, 0x0080553e vp44_sensor_diag_state_1, 0x00805540 fuel_arbitrator_rpm_target_history, 0x00805542 diagnostic_snapshot_zero_0, 0x00805544 diagnostic_snapshot_zero_1, 0x00805546 diagnostic_snapshot_zero_2, 0x00805548 fuel_arbitrator_rpm_history_index, 0x0080554a loop_counter_capture_start_2, 0x0080554e loop_counter_elapsed_time_2, 0x00805554 diagnostic_snapshot_position_flag, 0x00805555 diagnostic_snapshot_byte_1, 0x00805556 diagnostic_snapshot_fuel_mode_1, 0x00805558 vp44_sensor_diag_state_2, 0x0080555a fuel_arbitrator_state_history, 0x0080555c diagnostic_snapshot_zero_3, 0x0080555e diagnostic_snapshot_zero_4, 0x00805560 diagnostic_snapshot_zero_5.

e2m 10DA +118 DGRPOSFG 'fault log recording flag for engine speed overspeed error', the same record as CM848 engine_overspeed_log_entry_open_flag_cal. It is 1 while an engine_overspeed_log record is open: set when the latch sets with no record open, and cleared when the overspeed clears. 0x80553a + 0x118 = 0x805652. 17 CM550 e2m files carry this +118 variant, the one J90350.00's code uses. No _cal: it is in the flash parameter block, not the EEPROM mirror.

e2m 10DA +11A DGRPOSIN 'fault log index into engine speed overspeed error log' (0-4), the same record as CM848 engine_overspeed_log_index_cal. It selects the engine_overspeed_log record and advances modulo 5 when an overspeed ends. Only this function uses it. No _cal: flash parameter block.

e2m 0004 +0 CMECTR / RUN_TIME 'time key switch is on and ECM is running boot or application' (SEC, 0.2 s per count, 4 bytes), the same record as CM848 key_on_hour_meter. It has the same roles as in CM848: power-down and the restart through boot ROM save it to the EEPROM mirror (0x803b3e = EEPROM 0x34, as CM848 saves key_on_hour_meter to key_on_hour_meter_cal), and it is the fault timestamp clock, the security key time source and the overspeed log's start field. The 0004 -> 0x80bda4 mapping is from the frozen parameter_id_lookup_table.csv: the ROM formula only covers IDs from 0xfd1.

e2m 1096 +0 CKEGSRIH 'engine startup inhibit', the same record as CM848 engine_startup_inhibit_cal. While it is nonzero, STOPPED never moves to CRANKING. In CM550, vp44_validateRedundantSensors sets it at start-up when the parameter-block fault (word 0 bit 12) is active and confirmed and the 'run if power-down data lost' flag is 0. No _cal: 0x8057be is in the flash parameter block and recomputed at start-up, not in the EEPROM mirror.

Extra (droppable): it follows the 0x80d28c rename. It is the previous value of the shutdown command, copied from it at the end of processDiagnosticLimitStatus. That function uses it to count new shutdowns on the 0 -> 1 edge, and it is zeroed in STOPPED and by cm550_FUN_000192e0.

e2m 105E +14 CKEXES 'exit RPM for crank routine', the same record (mnemonic) as CM848 crank_exit_speed (105E +12 Crank_Exit_Speed [CKEXES]). CRANKING / JUMP_START / REENTRY move to RUNNING at it. CM550's table maps 105E to 0x80d098. It is not a source selector.

e2m 105E +12 CKREES 're-entry RPM for crank routine', the same record as CM848 crank_reentry_speed (105E +26 [CKREES]). RUNNING drops to REENTRY at or below it. cm550_peakTorqueFuelCorrection sets it to the crank initial reentry speed (105F +1C), plus the reentry offset (105F +1E) once the crank exit time has passed. Dump value 5200 = 650 rpm.

e2m 105E +8 CKJSTM 'timer used to dictate a jumpstart condition', the same record as CM848 crank_jump_start_timer (105E +24 [CKJSTM]). CRANKING moves to JUMP_START when it exceeds crank_jump_start_time. cm550_engineOperatingModeStateTrackingSlowCycle40Coordinator counts it.
e2m 105F +20 CKCNJSTM 'crank jumpstart time', the same record as CM848 crank_jump_start_time (105F +2A [CKCNJSTM]). It is the limit crank_jump_start_timer must pass before JUMP_START. Dump value 5.

e2m 117D +4 EBSS 'status of whether operating conditions indicate desire for brake activation', the same record as CM848 engine_retarder_active_flag (E_Brake_Status [EBSS]). RUNNING enters ENGINE_BRAKE while it is 1, and ENGINE_BRAKE returns to RUNNING when it is 0. The record identity is high confidence, but there is no writer in the dumped 256 KB (no absolute store, no store through the 117D base), so it is probably set by code above 0x40000.

e2m 1192 +C EBDLBKTY 'type of driveline brake (0 = exhaust / engine brake, 1 = retarder)', the same mnemonic as CM848 engine_brake_driveline_brake_type_cal (1180 +16 EB_Driveline_Brake_Type). CM550's table maps 1192 to EEPROM 0x10005aa, and +0xC = EEPROM 0x5b6 = mirror 0x803b0a + 0x5b6. Inside the EEPROM mirror, so _cal applies. ENGINE_BRAKE is entered only while it is 0, and in CM550 it must also be 0 to leave.

e2m 120C +4 SOKYSD, the same record as CM848 key_off_shutdown_mode (FSS_Key_Off_Shutdown [SOKYSD]). The CM550 e2m text is '0 = not used, 1 = shutdown from key-off in process, 2 = running normal'. The code uses it as CM848 does: 0 lets a key-off shut a running engine down, 1 forces SHUTDOWN from RUNNING and blocks both the return to STOPPED and the power-down start, 2 keeps a running engine running after key-off. Only initializeEngineState writes it (0).

New CM550 enum ENGINE_STATE, size 2, with CM848's member names. This member exists only for parity with CM848: no CM550 code in the dumped 256 KB compares with or stores 0. The switch default turns 0, or anything above 8, into STOPPED, and initializeEngineState stores 1 at start-up.

e2m 1068 FSEGST 1=STOP. Entered at or below engine_stopped_speed (from CRANKING / JUMP_START / REENTRY), from SHUTDOWN when the key is on again or a shutdown command ends at 0 rpm, by the default case and by initializeEngineState. It leaves to CRANKING above engine_stopped_speed while engine_startup_inhibit is 0. The RAM dump holds 1.
e2m 2=CRANK. Entered from STOPPED. It leaves to RUNNING at crank_exit_speed, to JUMP_START when crank_jump_start_timer exceeds crank_jump_start_time, and to STOPPED at engine_stopped_speed.
e2m 3=RUN. Entered at crank_exit_speed from CRANKING / JUMP_START / REENTRY, and from ENGINE_BRAKE / OVERSPEED when their condition ends.
e2m 4=ENGBRAKE. Entered from RUNNING while engine_retarder_active_flag (117D +4 EBSS) is 1 and engine_brake_driveline_brake_type_cal is 0. It returns to RUNNING when both are 0.
e2m 5=OVERSPED. Entered from RUNNING while engine_overspeed_active_flag is 1. It returns to RUNNING when the flag clears.
e2m 6=JUMPSTRT. Entered from CRANKING after crank_jump_start_timer passes crank_jump_start_time. It leaves like CRANKING, without the jump start test. The consumers treat it like CRANKING.
e2m 7=REENTRY. Entered from RUNNING when engine_rpm_primary falls to crank_reentry_speed. It leaves like JUMP_START: to RUNNING at crank_exit_speed, to STOPPED at engine_stopped_speed.

e2m 8=SHUTDOWN. Entered when the key switch (SWITCHES bit 0) is off without key_off_shutdown_inhibit_flag (from every state except RUNNING, where key_off_shutdown_mode 0 is also needed), when key_off_shutdown_mode is 1 (from RUNNING), or when engine_shutdown_command_flag is 1. At 0 rpm with the key off, no inhibit and mode not 1, it sets power_down_start_flag. It returns to STOPPED when the key is on or the command ends at 0 rpm, unless key_off_shutdown_mode is 1.

There are 35 absolute cmpi.w #N,$80d0c8 and 1 move.w #1 store, 13 functions that use it through an address register (byte-scanned: cmpi.w #N,(An) and move.w #N,(An) only), the switch read, and 2 copies into previous-state words. The output image of the SIM Port E pins, and an output request byte. It is e2m 000E +2A, byte 2 (outputs 16-23) of the 6-byte output image array 0x80bcf6-0x80bcfb. mc68k_ioDriverStrobeHandler writes it to SIM_PORTE0 with bit 5 inverted. Each writer sets or clears its bit only while that output's override slot (0x80bd1a + output number) is 0, then calls the strobe handler. The old name is the e2m text of one bit only. Bits: (mask 0x02) boot block programming enable (SSBBPGEA), set only around the boot block erase / program. (mask 0x04) flash programming enable (SSVTEA 'bit which allows the processor to enable flash programming'), on from the start of the power-down saves to their end, around every flash erase / program (parameter blocks 0x4000 / 0x6000 and the boot block). (mask 0x08) the ECM power hold, MEDIUM confidence by role: the boot block sets this pin first after reset, the application main sets it, and the power-down clears it after the saves and sets it again if the ECM is still running or the key comes back. Those are the steps CM848's cm848_runPowerDownSequence runs on logical output 27. (mask 0x10) set at the output start-up and cleared just before restartThroughBootRom jumps into the boot ROM; what it drives is not proven. (mask 0x20) driven inverted at the pin. Typed byte, not a bitfield struct (CM550 has none yet).

TWIN (one shared name, a row in each firmware). Both bodies are the same three steps in the same order: compare the message object number argument (zero-extended low byte) with the J1939 transmit object number word (CM550 0x80d9f4 / CM848 0x40ad68); equal -> send the next queued J1939 frame (CM550 mc68k_canCs4TransmitNextFrame 0x1e52e / CM848 mpc555_processJ1939TxBufferSend 0x535e8, hardware counterparts with the same steps: completed flag = 1, reset the object interrupt, ring empty and not full -> stop the object, else copy the next entry, clear the full flag, advance the ring with wrap, then the cannot-transmit fault clear); else -> the verified twin hook ignoreCanTransmitInterrupt (CM550 0xc80c / CM848 0x26f78) with the object number still as its argument (CM550 pushes it as a word; CM848 leaves it in r3). Same role: the only caller of each is the transmit branch of the J1939 CAN controller interrupt handler (CM550 mc68k_canCs4InterruptHandler bsr.w at 0x1e134 for an object whose 82527 control 0 TXIE bit 5 is set; CM848 mpc555_canTransmitInterruptHandler bl at 0x53bf0 for the mailbox equal to the transmit index), and each is the sole caller of its transmit-next function. The index global is set the same way at start-up in both (last message object used + 1; the receive objects are index + 1 .. last + 15). The dispatch test differs (hardware: TXIE vs index compare), the handler does not. The one encoding difference is the ABI of a byte parameter: CM550's callee takes the low byte of the 2-byte stack slot (moveq #0 ; move.b d2,d0), CM848's caller clears the upper bits (clrlwi r3,r4,24 at 0x53bec). Name it after the hook pair: handle (this) / ignore (ignoreCanTransmitInterrupt), with J1939 to set it apart from CM550 vp44_handleCanCs5TransmitInterrupt.
